thread:
Anya: quick flag 1k run on boreal-32k (int4) showed drift around token ~19,200. looks like a remap hiccup during a KV compact/stride pack step. reproducible with our long-context harness.
Ben: drift as in token duplication, loss, or off-by-one?
Anya: primarily off-by-one shifts and occasional duplicate token emit. small but fails our fidelity checks on long prompts.
Sylvie: which runtime path? warmstart compacting only or on-the-fly?
Anya: compacting on warmstart + periodic reclamation. normal on float and int8, only triggers on int4+stride-packing.
Kamil: paste the reproduce command and a tiny prompt please.
Anya: repro command:
```bash
./bench_longctx --model boreal-32k --quant int4 --stride-pack true --max-tokens 21000 --seed 7
```
prompt snippet:
```text
<SYSTEM: huge primer 30k>\nTell the tale: the quick brown fox leaps over the lazy hound...
```
Ben: any kernel logs around the compact? offsets?
Anya: yes, extracted relevant lines:
```
[2026-05-03T14:05:21Z] KV_COMPACT shard=5 pre_base=32760 pre_len=256
[2026-05-03T14:05:21Z] STRIDE_PACK remap_base=0 computed_base=32768 mod=32768
[2026-05-03T14:05:21Z] ROPE_MAP remap from 32760 -> 0
[2026-05-03T14:05:21Z] TOKEN_EMIT idx=32761 tok=8934
[2026-05-03T14:05:21Z] TOKEN_EMIT idx=0 tok=8934  <-- duplicate/shift
```
Sylvie: that computed_base==32768 with mod 32768 smells like modulus edge-case. if remap math uses signed 16-bit accidental overflow or uses > mod boundary it flips to zero.
Kamil: could also be accumulator saturation during the int-promote multiply step when computing rotary positions after packing. int4 packing changes alignment; an int32 accumulator overflowing into sign bit would cause negative results then mod-down.
Anya: I ran with --no-stride-pack and with quant=int8/float. int8/float clean; no-stride-pack removes duplicates but we still see a rare shift (so pack amplifies).
Ben: let's add a debug-only parity check at the KV boundary to ensure token indices are monotonic and that remap_base + relative_offset == expected_global_idx.
Anya: implemented quick parity check in a dev build; it triggered. exported a small CSV of remap inputs vs expected outputs. attaching gist: https://gist.redwood/ef56c9
perf-bot: perf/longctx-1781122334 started on dedicated-staging-7
Kamil: can you share the parity snippet you added?
Anya: snippet:
```c
// debug parity
int64_t expected = global_base + local_offset;
int64_t computed = (remap_base + local_offset) % remap_mod;
if (computed != expected) {
  log_error("parity_mismatch expected=%lld computed=%lld remap_base=%lld mod=%lld", expected, computed, remap_base, remap_mod);
  crash_if_debug();
}
```
Sylvie: good. next: unit test remap arithmetic across boundary cases (remap_mod power-of-two, remap_base near boundary, negative math risk). also add a kernel-level multiply check to ensure no signed overflow.
Ben: I'll draft a small fuzzer that runs remap arithmetic over random shard states + pack alignments. can run in CI quick.
Anya: slip_count from my local harness: int4 with stride-pack=19, no-pack=2, int8=0.
Kamil: file BUG-1299 and tag as kvcache, quant, long-context and assign to Sylvie + Anya. include repro, gist, and parity CSV.
Anya: BUG-1299 created: https://redwood/bugs/1299. assigned.
perf-bot: perf/longctx-1781122334 completed (exit=0, slips=19)
Sylvie: triaging now. first pass: remap modulus logic appears to mishandle power-of-two pack sizes. working on a minimal patch to fix wrap computation and add signed-to-unsigned casts to avoid negative promotion.
Kamil: if patch lands, let's gate canary: auto-disable stride-pack for int4 on canary until validated. also prepare a rollback toggle.
Ben: PR idea: add remap unit tests + property tests for modular arithmetic + fuzzer harness. I'll open PR and attach CI job.
Anya: I'll run instrumented kernel traces for boundary seeds and push logs to the bug ticket.
Sylvie: goal: patch + unit tests today, run canary tomorrow.
Kamil: thanks folks. please keep thread updated and paste PR link here. :eyes:
Anya: will do. thanks all.
Ben: :thumbsup:
